newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday were light at $66.00 per cwt and passed by owners asking $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of last week's cattle sold at $68.00 before prices slipped to $67.00 in light trade Thursday and Friday.
Some cattle feeders said they expect sales by Wednesday at $67.00, provided beef prices hold firm and owners remain resolute in their attempts to get packers to raise bids, they said.
Beef prices Monday were quoted up $0.28 to $0.52 per cwt, with 193 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Texas Panhandle-area feedlots continued to dry out following heavy rain and snow Friday, but remained sloppy in some areas, several sources there said.
Death loss at feedlots was minimal from the storm, with already weakened or sick animals more susceptible than healthy, market-ready cattle, they said.
Losses of lightweight calves just shipped in from Mexico or south Texas that were already weak or not acclimated occured to some extent, cattle sources said.
Cattle on grass in the Hereford-Amarillo area were being rounded up to assess the toll taken by the storm, they said.
""We always lose some weak cattle when we have a storm like that," said Kenneth Chambers, a field inspector for the Texas and Southwestern Cattle Raisers.
